name: Herbal/botanical infusions
anchor: Per-form sovereign beverage cells in the as-consumed liquid basis (EU 2023/915 juice and rice-drink cells, Codex CXS 193 fruit juices, EU 2024/1987 beverage nickel, EU canned-beverage tin, Hong Kong Cap 132V's named carbonated, tea, coffee and wine beverage entries, and the US and Hong Kong packaged-drinking-water quality standards), with dry leaf, bean and powder commodities anchored separately in their own as-sold basis and never converted between the two
native_basis_label: dry botanical as sold (loose material, tea bags, sachets, pyramids), reported on the as-sold dry article; this is the lot the applicant packages and the auditor samples
scope_note: Dried botanical infusion material other than Camellia sinensis, as sold: chamomile, peppermint, spearmint, rooibos, honeybush, hibiscus, lemongrass, lemon balm, ginger, liquorice root, chrysanthemum, kuding (broadleaf holly leaf), yerba mate, guayusa and blends of those, in loose and bagged formats. Camellia sinensis material routes to the true-tea row and matcha to the matcha row. An infusion carrying a Supplement Facts panel routes to Category 16 (Dietary Supplements) by the taxonomy boundary rule, which removes most single-herb medicinal preparations from this row. A ready-to-drink bottled herbal infusion is a different product form in a different basis: it is assessed in the as-consumed liquid basis against the applicable ready-to-drink beverage cell, never by applying this row's dry-material ceiling to a brewed liquid, and never by applying a ready-to-drink ceiling to this row's dry material.
basis_guard: as[ _]sold|product as placed on market|edible part|dry matter|dry weight
basis_guard_note: This row publishes a dry-commodity ceiling in the as-sold basis (the article the applicant packages and the lot the auditor samples), so every named anchor must itself be a dry-commodity as-sold or as-placed-on-market cell. The guard refuses the ready-to-drink beverage cells: Hong Kong Cap 132V Note 11 restricts its beverage entries to beverages that are, or are reconstituted to be, ready to drink, and applying a ready-to-drink ceiling to a dry leaf, bean or powder would be a basis conflation in the strict direction, not a standard.
method: HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit-only): the strictest applicable sovereign maximum level for this exact beverage form and analyte in the row's declared native basis, with disclosed read-across where the exact cell is unregulated, a substantiated not-material determination where a species is bounded or is a method artifact, and a control where no defensible sovereign number and no supportable near-neighbour exist. Never occurrence-derived. Ready-to-drink and dry-commodity bases are never mixed and no brewing, dilution or reconstitution factor is invented.

Pb.basis: as sold, dry botanical material (read across from the Hong Kong named infusion-botanical cells)
Pb.label: No credible sovereign has written a general lead maximum level for dried herbal or botanical infusion material. Hong Kong Cap 132V is the only credible instrument that reaches this commodity class at all, and it does so through two named botanicals: Broadleaf Holly leaves at 2000 ug/kg and Dried chrysanthemum at 5000 ug/kg, both as sold. The stricter of the two named infusion-botanical cells (2000 ug/kg) is adopted by disclosed read-across as the row ceiling.
Pb.substantiation: The read-across is within a commodity class and within a single instrument's own schedule: both named cells are dried leaf or flower material sold to be infused, in the as-sold dry basis this row publishes, so no basis treatment is required. Taking 2000 rather than 5000 is deliberate: a chrysanthemum infusion is held to the stricter of the two values its own regulator wrote for neighbouring botanicals, which is over-compliance in that one case and is disclosed here. The alternative anchors were all rejected on applicability: the Camellia sinensis cell (5000 ug/kg) is scoped to true tea, which this row excludes; the EU dried-spice cells (fruit spices 600 ug/kg, root and rhizome spices 1500 ug/kg) are written for material ingested whole as a seasoning, not infused and discarded; the ready-to-drink beverage cells are in the wrong basis. Non-credible-tier instruments that do address this class directly (Israel and MERCOSUR raw tea and plants for infusion at 5000 and 600 ug/kg) sit outside the credible-regulator set and were not used, and the absence of an EU or Codex cell for herbal infusions is recorded as a register and regulatory gap rather than filled by an occurrence value.

Cd.rationale: No credible sovereign sets a cadmium maximum level for dried herbal or botanical infusion material. Hong Kong Cap 132V, the only credible instrument that names infusion botanicals at all, sets lead values for them but no cadmium value; EU 2023/915, Codex CXS 193, FSANZ Schedule 19 and Health Canada set no cadmium cell for herbal infusions or for tea. Two EU cells reach the nearest commodities and both were considered and rejected: the leaf-vegetable cadmium cell (100 ug/kg, eu2023_cd_leaf_vegetables_100) and the spinaches, similar leaves, mustard seedlings and fresh herbs cell (200 ug/kg, eu2023_cd_spinach_herbs_200), which is the closest sovereign cadmium cell to this commodity that exists. Both are fresh-weight edible-portion values for a plant eaten whole while fresh, and carrying either onto a dried botanical sold as sold would require an invented drying factor of roughly an order of magnitude; the register records both on a wet-weight basis and this row's basis guard refuses them for that reason. No near-neighbour read-across is supportable, so the fail-safe disposition is a control: cadmium testing is mandatory on every certified lot and no ceiling is invented from occurrence data.
Cd.reference_method: Cadmium by ICP-MS on every certified lot, reported on the certificate. A result above 10 ug/kg in a ready-to-drink form, or above 100 ug/kg in a dry form, escalates to an ingredient-origin and process-water investigation and is a Standards Ratchet surveillance input under Governance Policy section 12.

companions.scope: spinaches and similar leaves, mustard seedlings, and fresh herbs

tAs.rationale: No credible sovereign sets a total-arsenic maximum level for dried herbal or botanical infusion material. Regulators write beverage arsenic limits on the inorganic species (EU 2023/915 section 3.4.4 fruit juices at 20 ug/kg and section 3.4.1.6 non-alcoholic rice-based drinks at 30 ug/kg; the US FDA apple-juice action level at 10 ug/kg) and write unspeciated arsenic limits only in the packaged-water and public-water-supply schedules, which are Category 8 instruments. No sovereign writes an inorganic-arsenic cell for this commodity either, so both arsenic cells in this row are controls and the escalation rule carries the obligation. Total arsenic is therefore mandatory on every lot as the parent screen and no total-arsenic ceiling is invented.
tAs.reference_method: Total arsenic by ICP-MS on every certified lot. Inorganic-arsenic speciation (HPLC-ICP-MS) is reflexed whenever total arsenic exceeds 50 percent of this row's inorganic-arsenic ceiling, or 20 ug/kg where this row publishes no inorganic-arsenic number. Species never substitute for the total: the iAs result does not satisfy the tAs reporting requirement.

iAs.rationale: No credible sovereign sets an inorganic-arsenic maximum level for dried herbal or botanical infusion material. Every sovereign inorganic-arsenic cell is scoped either to rice and rice-based products, to a ready-to-drink beverage (EU fruit juices 20 ug/kg, EU non-alcoholic rice-based drinks 30 ug/kg, US FDA apple juice 10 ug/kg), to seafood, or to packaged and public drinking water. None of those is applicable to this dry commodity, and applying a ready-to-drink beverage cell to a dry leaf, bean or powder would be a basis conflation. Inorganic arsenic is a Tier-1 analyte, so it is speciated whenever the total-arsenic screen is elevated.
iAs.reference_method: Inorganic arsenic by HPLC-ICP-MS, reflexed whenever total arsenic on the lot exceeds 100 ug/kg in the as-sold dry basis; a confirmed inorganic-arsenic result escalates to an origin and irrigation-water investigation. Inorganic arsenic never substitutes for the total-arsenic report.

tHg.rationale: No credible sovereign sets a total-mercury maximum level for dried herbal or botanical infusion material. The sovereign mercury values in this basis family are the packaged-drinking-water quality standards (US 21 CFR 165.110 total mercury at 2 ug/kg; Hong Kong Cap 132V packaged drinking water, written for inorganic mercury at 6 ug/kg) and the fish and seafood methylmercury and total-mercury ceilings, none of which governs this product form. Mercury has no identified enrichment pathway in this supply chain, but the analyte is on the mandatory eight-total panel, so testing is mandatory and no ceiling is invented.
tHg.reference_method: Total mercury by ICP-MS (or dedicated amalgamation AAS) on every certified lot, reported on the certificate. A detection above 5 ug/kg escalates to an ingredient and process-water investigation and reflexes methylmercury speciation.

MeHg.rationale: Methylmercury has no formation pathway in a dried botanical infusion material: there is no marine bioaccumulation step in the supply chain and no anaerobic, sulfate-reducing methylation environment in the product or its process. Methylmercury is a component of total mercury (MeHg <= tHg) and is governed by and bounded by the total-mercury cell; no separate methylmercury ceiling is published.
MeHg.reference_method: Bounded by the total-mercury cell (tHg). Methylmercury speciation (HPLC-ICP-MS or GC-ICP-MS) is reflexed only on an elevated total-mercury result; it is not a routine lot test for this form.
MeHg.regulatory_basis: No credible sovereign sets a methylmercury limit for any beverage, leaf, bean or beverage powder. Methylmercury maximum levels are scoped to fish, seafood and other marine matrices (EU 2023/915 section 3.3, US FDA CPG 540.600, Hong Kong Cap 132V fish entries). Methylmercury is a species of and bounded by total mercury (MeHg <= tHg), which this row controls directly.
MeHg.jurisdictions_checked: EU 2023/915 (and EU 2024/1987 for nickel, EU 2025/1891 for arsenic in seafood); Codex CXS 193-1995; US FDA (21 CFR 165.110 bottled-water quality standards, Juice HACCP guidance, Closer to Zero action levels); FSANZ Food Standards Code Schedule 19; Health Canada List of Contaminants and Other Adulterating Substances; UK retained maximum levels; Hong Kong Cap 132V (Food Adulteration (Metallic Contamination) Regulations) — none sets a methylmercury limit for this product form.

Ni.rationale: No credible sovereign sets a nickel maximum level for dried herbal or botanical infusion material. EU 2024/1987 is the only comprehensive sovereign nickel instrument; its cells cover cereals, pulses, oilseeds, tree nuts, vegetables, cocoa and chocolate, infant formula, baby food and fruit and vegetable juices, and none of them is written for dried infusion material. The two cells that come closest are named and rejected rather than passed over: the fresh-herbs cell (1200 ug/kg, eu2024_ni_fresh_herbs_1200) and the leafy-vegetables-except-fresh-herbs cell (500 ug/kg, eu2024_ni_leafy_veg_500). Both are recorded in the register on a wet-weight basis for a plant sold fresh, and this row certifies the dried commodity as sold, so adopting either would require a drying factor that no instrument supplies; this row's basis guard refuses them on that ground. The juice and nectar cell (250 ug/kg) is written in a ready-to-drink basis and cannot be applied to a dry commodity, and the dry-commodity cells that do exist are written for other plant families. Nickel is a Tier-2 analyte on the mandatory eight-total panel.
Ni.reference_method: Total nickel by ICP-MS on every certified lot in the as-sold dry basis, reported on the certificate. An elevated result escalates to a soil, cultivar and stainless-equipment investigation.

Sn.rationale: No credible sovereign sets a tin maximum level for dried herbal or botanical infusion material. The exclusion is written into the instrument itself: EU 2023/915 Annex I section 3.5 scopes its inorganic-tin maximum levels to canned beverages and canned foods and expressly excepts canned dried and canned powdered products, and the Codex, FSANZ and Hong Kong canned-food cells carry the same carve-out. There is therefore no sovereign number for a dry beverage commodity and no supportable read-across, because the canned-liquid cells are written in a ready-to-drink basis. Tin is nonetheless on the mandatory eight-total panel.
Sn.reference_method: Total tin by ICP-MS on every certified lot in the as-sold dry basis, reported on the certificate. Where the applicant also sells a canned ready-to-drink form of this product, that form is verified separately against the canned-beverage tin maximum level in the as-consumed basis.

companions.scope: canned beverages, including canned fruit and vegetable juices, except ca

Al.rationale: No credible sovereign sets an aluminium maximum level for dried herbal or botanical infusion material, and no near-neighbour read-across is supportable: the only sovereign aluminium values are packaged-drinking-water quality standards written in a litre-of-water basis (Category 8) and the FSANZ infant-formula limits (Category 1). Applying a water-basis value to a dry commodity would be a basis conflation of roughly three orders of magnitude. Aluminium is a live cell for this row and is not treated as a formality: several infusion botanicals are aluminium accumulators, and no credible sovereign has set a ceiling, so the analyte is reported on every certified lot and the gap is disclosed on the certificate rather than papered over with a number HMTc would have had to invent.
Al.reference_method: Total aluminium by ICP-MS on every certified lot, reported on the certificate in the as-sold dry basis. A result that departs materially from the applicant's own documented origin and process baseline escalates to a soil, cultivar and processing-aid investigation. This is a process-control tripwire, not a numeric standard: no ceiling is published because no credible sovereign maximum exists for this cell.

Cr.rationale: No credible sovereign sets a total-chromium maximum level for dried herbal or botanical infusion material. The only sovereign chromium values reachable from this basis family are the packaged-drinking-water quality standards (US 21 CFR 165.110 at 100 ug/kg, Hong Kong Cap 132V packaged drinking water at 50 ug/kg), which govern water sold as water and are Category 8 instruments, and the public-water-system maximum contaminant levels (US EPA, Health Canada), which are water-utility instruments and not food law at all. Total chromium in this form is dominated by benign Cr(III) and is reported as a stainless-steel equipment and process-water leaching screen, not as a health limit; the health-relevant species is addressed in the Cr-VI cell.
Cr.reference_method: Total chromium by ICP-MS on every certified lot, reported on the certificate. An elevated result triggers the Cr(VI) speciation reflex and an equipment, process-water and ingredient investigation.

Cr-VI.rationale: No credible sovereign sets a hexavalent-chromium limit for any food or beverage, and the in-matrix reduction argument that supports a not-material determination in an acidic beverage is not available here: this row's certified article is a DRY botanical solid, so there is no aqueous matrix in which Cr(VI) could be reduced to Cr(III), and the acidic-beverage reduction argument is simply unavailable. Because Cr(VI) cannot be assumed to be reduced to Cr(III) in this matrix, the fail-safe disposition is a control rather than a not-material determination, and no ceiling is invented.
Cr-VI.reference_method: Total chromium by ICP-MS on every certified lot. Cr(VI)-specific speciation (IC-ICP-MS, EN 15192 adapted) is reflexed whenever total chromium exceeds 100 ug/kg in this form, or 50 percent of the total-chromium screen value where this row publishes one. A confirmed Cr(VI) detection escalates to a process-water, equipment and ingredient investigation and blocks certification pending resolution.
